label: History
value: Anne Shirley was orphaned in infancy in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Orphaned in infancy in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne Shirley spent her early childhood in the care of guardians before being brought to Prince Edward Island to live with Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert at Green Gables. Though taken in by mistake instead of a boy, she quickly won over her guardians and settled into Avonlea. She attended local school, where she formed a close bond with Diana Barry and established a intense academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe after he called her 'Carrots.' Throughout her school years, she repeatedly found herself in dramatic scrapes, such as accidentally dying her hair green and baking a cake with wrong ingredients. She won the Avery Scholarship at Queen's Academy, but chose to stay at Green Gables and teach locally to support Marilla. Later, she co-founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and helped reunite her friend Miss Lavendar with Stephen Irving. Eventually, Anne left Avonlea to pursue her Arts degree at Redmond College in Kingsport, where she excelled in English and began publishing her writings. During her college years, she rejected marriage proposals from Billy Andrews and Gilbert Blythe, and entered into a romantic courtship with Royal Gardner while remaining deeply attached to her Island home.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye was taken in as an orphan.
unit: Anthony Pye was taken in as an orphan nephew by Mrs. George Pye and subsequently enrolled as a student at Avonlea school under Anne Shirley. From his very first day, he held an antagonistic attitude toward Anne, remarking that she was no good because she was a female teacher. He engaged in disruptive behavior, such as pouring water down Aurelia Clay's neck and putting a live mouse in Anne's desk drawer. After the mouse incident, Anne lost her temper and whipped him with a hardwood pointer until he winced and cried. Surprisingly, this punishment gained Anthony's respect, causing him to offer to carry Anne's books the next morning and declare that her whipping was as effective as a man's. When Anne later resigned from teaching at Avonlea, Anthony fought two pitched battles with other boys to relieve his upset feelings.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father.
unit: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, who drowned shortly before her birth. After her daughter married and departed for foreign mission work, she found herself lonely in her large home. When Philippa Gordon proposed renting a house in Kingsport for college, Aunt Jamesina moved in to serve as housekeeper for Philippa, Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Stella Maynard at Patty's Place. She brought along her two cats, the Sarah-cat and Joseph, and later helped care for the stray cat Rusty. She remained at Patty's Place during holidays to tend to the cats and house plants. When the girls graduated from Redmond College, she decided to take all three cats home with her so they would not be separated.

label: History
value: Billy grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Billy grew up in Avonlea as part of the prominent Andrews family. He drove Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and his sister Jane to a concert at the White Sands Hotel, where he sat in wait for them during the event due to his extreme shyness. Deeply admiring Anne Shirley, he watched her quietly for years at social gatherings like school parties. When his father deeded the upper farm to him in his own name, Billy wished to marry Anne but was too shy to court her himself. He persuaded his sister Jane to propose to Anne on his behalf, offering to wait until she finished college. After Anne refused him, he turned his affections to Nettie Blewett, whom he subsequently married and brought to live on his family's pew in Avonlea.

Deeply admiring Anne Shirley, he watched her quietly for years at social gatherings like school parties. When his father deeded the upper farm to him in his own name, Billy wished to marry Anne but was too shy to court her himself. He persuaded his sister Jane to propose to Anne on his behalf, offering to wait until she finished college. After Anne refused him, he turned his affections to Nettie Blewett, whom he subsequently married and brought to live on his family's pew in Avonlea.

label: History
value: Charlotta the Fourth went to live at Echo Lodge.
unit: Charlotta the Fourth went to live at Echo Lodge as a young teenager to serve as a handmaiden for Miss Lavendar Lewis. She quickly formed a deep attachment to her mistress, keeping her company and indulging her imaginative pretense without judgment. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally discovered Echo Lodge, Charlotta welcomed them warmly and was thrilled by Anne's grace, continually practicing in front of a mirror to mimic Anne's mannerisms. She worried greatly over Miss Lavendar's mood and health, confiding her fears to Anne. When Stephen Irving returned to propose to Miss Lavendar, Charlotta was intensely excited, helping Anne manage the household and watching over the romance. She eagerly assisted with the wedding preparations and served at the outdoor ceremony in late August. Following the wedding, Charlotta moved to Boston with Mr. and Mrs. Irving and Paul, though she felt terribly homesick at first. She returned to Echo Lodge with the family during subsequent summer vacations, having grown into a young lady.

She quickly formed a deep attachment to her mistress, keeping her company and indulging her imaginative pretense without judgment. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally discovered Echo Lodge, Charlotta welcomed them warmly and was thrilled by Anne's grace, continually practicing in front of a mirror to mimic Anne's mannerisms. She worried greatly over Miss Lavendar's mood and health, confiding her fears to Anne. When Stephen Irving returned to propose to Miss Lavendar, Charlotta was intensely excited, helping Anne manage the household and watching over the romance. She eagerly assisted with the wedding preparations and served at the outdoor ceremony in late August. Following the wedding, Charlotta moved to Boston with Mr. and Mrs. Irving and Paul, though she felt terribly homesick at first. She returned to Echo Lodge with the family during subsequent summer vacations, having grown into a young lady.

label: History
value: Davy's mother died
unit: Following the death of his sick mother, Davy and his twin sister Dora were brought from East Grafton to Green Gables by Marilla Cuthbert. From his arrival, he engaged in constant antics, such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck at church, placing a toad in Marilla's bed, locking Dora in a dark shed, and squashing lemon pies. Under Anne Shirley's affectionate guidance, his behavior gradually improved after he learned that lying and misbehaving were wrong. When his uncle Richard Keith passed away, money was left in trust for Davy and Dora, allowing them to remain permanently at Green Gables. He enrolled at the Avonlea school, becoming fast friends with Milty Boulter and competing with his peers while growing taller.

From his arrival, he engaged in constant antics, such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck at church, placing a toad in Marilla's bed, locking Dora in a dark shed, and squashing lemon pies. Under Anne Shirley's affectionate guidance, his behavior gradually improved after he learned that lying and misbehaving were wrong. When his uncle Richard Keith passed away, money was left in trust for Davy and Dora, allowing them to remain permanently at Green Gables. He enrolled at the Avonlea school, becoming fast friends with Milty Boulter and competing with his peers while growing taller.

label: History
value: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley
unit: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley when Anne moves to Green Gables, and the two immediately swear an oath of eternal friendship. Shortly after, during a tea party at Green Gables, Diana accidentally becomes drunk when Anne unknowingly serves her currant wine instead of raspberry cordial, causing Mrs. Barry to strictly forbid them from seeing each other. Diana secretly keeps in touch until she falls gravely ill with croup during a night her parents are away; Anne nurses Diana's little sister Minnie May through the night, winning Mrs. Barry's forgiveness and restoring their friendship. Together, the two create playhouses, form a story club, and go on trips, including an exciting visit to Charlottetown hosted by Diana's wealthy aunt, Miss Josephine Barry. Unlike Anne, Diana does not attend Queen's Academy because her parents choose not to send her. She later becomes engaged to Fred Wright, whom she marries, eventually settling into domestic life and giving birth to her firstborn child.

label: History
value: Following the death of her mother, Dora and Davy were brought to Green Gables.
unit: Following the death of her mother, Dora and her twin brother Davy were brought to Green Gables to be taken in by Marilla Cuthbert. Unlike her mischievous brother, Dora proved to be extraordinarily quiet, polite, and helpful from the start. Shortly after arriving, she was led onto a pigpen fence by Davy, fell in, and was thoroughly soaked when he tried to wash her under the pump. On another occasion, she was locked in a toolhouse by Davy, who then falsely claimed she was lost. Despite Davy's frequent tricks and pranks, Dora remained well-behaved and dutiful, helping Marilla with chores around the house and garden. She began attending school alongside Davy under Anne Shirley's instruction. Upon the death of her uncle Richard Keith, a trust fund was established for Dora and Davy, securing their permanent home at Green Gables. During a severe hailstorm, Dora remained composed and prayed silently alongside Anne. At age eight, when Anne departed for Redmond College, Dora handled the farewell calmly and continued her studies at Sunday School and home under the care of Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde.

label: Quotes
value: > I’m awfully sorry I made fun of your hair, Anne. Honest I am. Don’t be mad for keeps, now.

label: Quotes
value: > I’ll never ask you to be friends again, Anne Shirley. And I don’t care either!

label: Quotes
value: > It wasn’t particularly good of me at all, Anne. I was pleased to be able to do you some small service. Are we going to be friends after this? Have you really forgiven me my old fault?

label: Quotes
value: > We are going to be the best of friends. We were born to be good friends, Anne. You’ve thwarted destiny enough. I know we can help each other in many ways. You are going to keep up your studies, aren’t you? So am I. Come, I’m going to walk home with you.

label: Quotes
value: > Friends! Your friendship can’t satisfy me, Anne. I want your love—and you tell me I can never have that.

value: Gilbert is a handsome boy

value: Gilbert is cheerful
unit: Gilbert is cheerful, clever, and inherently ambitious, constantly determined to excel in his studies and make the best out of life. In his academic and personal life, he shows deep perseverance, strategic leadership, and high ideals.

label: History
value: Gilbert pulled Anne Shirley's hair.
unit: Upon returning to Avonlea school, Gilbert inadvertently sparked a long feud with Anne Shirley by pulling her hair and calling her 'Carrots', receiving a broken slate over his head in response. Despite his immediate and sincere apologies, Anne refused to speak to him or forgive him for years, sparking a fierce academic rivalry throughout their time at Avonlea school and Queen's Academy. After Gilbert won the Medal at Queen's, he surrendered his appointment as teacher at the Avonlea school so that Anne could remain close to home following Matthew Cuthbert's death, leading Anne to finally forgive him and initiate a close friendship. Gilbert went on to teach at White Sands while serving as president of the Avonlea Village Improvement Society before attending Redmond College to pursue a career as a doctor. At Redmond, he distinguished himself as freshman class president, joined the 'Lambs' fraternity, and earned high academic honors. During his sophomore year at Redmond, Gilbert confessed his love to Anne at Patty's Place, but she rejected his proposal, after which he respectfully retreated into a distant, polite friendship. Overworking himself in pursuit of honors and the Cooper Prize, Gilbert fell critically ill with typhoid fever after his junior year, but survived and resumed his warm comradeship with Anne.

He initially clashed with Anne Shirley after finding her Jersey cow in his oat field, but after Anne mistakenly sold his cow and brought him a homemade cake as a peace offering, the two became close friends. When lightning struck his house and killed his troublesome parrot Ginger, Anne came to comfort him in his grief. Shortly afterward, his estranged wife Emily arrived in Avonlea following a comedic misunderstanding involving a published newspaper joke, leading the pair to reconcile and restore order to his household. Mr. Harrison remained a supportive friend and literary critic for Anne during her writing endeavors, providing pragmatic advice on her stories.

label: History
value: Jane grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school as a classmate and friend of Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Ruby Gillis. She participated in various local events, including school concerts and the girls' Story Club, where her contributions were noted for being practical and lacking romance. She joined the Queen's preparation class under Miss Stacy and attended Queen's Academy, where she excelled in domestic science and obtained her teacher's license. Following graduation, she taught school in Newbridge, earning a place on the School Inspector's Roll of Honor. During her time as a teacher, she was an active member of the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Later, she taught school on the western prairies. While visiting Anne over a holiday break, Jane proposed to Anne on behalf of her shy brother Billy, though Anne declined. In time, Jane became engaged to Edward Inglis, an English millionaire from Winnipeg, whom she married in Avonlea before moving to Winnipeg and traveling to Europe.

label: History
value: Josie Pye frequently caused friction among her classmates at school in Avonlea.
unit: At school in Avonlea, Josie Pye frequently caused friction among her classmates. She once peeped at her book during a spelling lesson and sneered at Anne Shirley during various punishments. During a gathering, after showing off her skill walking a board fence, she dared Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, which resulted in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. During preparations for a school concert, Josie became sulky when she was not cast as the fairy queen in a dialogue. She later joined the Queen's Academy preparation class, where she openly boasted that she only sought higher education for its own sake rather than to earn a living. She successfully passed the Entrance examinations, scraping through with three marks to spare. While studying at Queen's Academy in Kingsport, she gained a reputation as the sharpest-tongued young lady in attendance. Following graduation from Queen's, she chose to return for another year of study rather than teach, and her home hosted a farewell party hosted by the Avonlea Victoria Improvement Society.

During preparations for a school concert, Josie became sulky when she was not cast as the fairy queen in a dialogue. She later joined the Queen's Academy preparation class, where she openly boasted that she only sought higher education for its own sake rather than to earn a living. She successfully passed the Entrance examinations, scraping through with three marks to spare. While studying at Queen's Academy in Kingsport, she gained a reputation as the sharpest-tongued young lady in attendance. Following graduation from Queen's, she chose to return for another year of study rather than teach, and her home hosted a farewell party hosted by the Avonlea Victoria Improvement Society.

label: Personality
value: Lavendar is romantic
unit: Miss Lavendar is romantic, imaginative, and youthful at heart, loving to play pretend and make-believe as if she were a young girl. Though hospitable, sweet, and sympathetic, she possesses a proud, sulky streak that once ruined her early romance. She enjoys quiet seclusion, loves young people, and admits to a playful fondness for indigestible treats.

label: History
value: Miss Lavendar lived isolated at Echo Lodge in Grafton
unit: Miss Lavendar lived isolated at Echo Lodge in Grafton for decades following a broken engagement with Stephen Irving. She maintained a quiet, imaginative lifestyle with her young handmaiden, Charlotta the Fourth, playing pretend tea parties and entertaining imaginary companions. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry stumbled upon her home, Miss Lavendar formed an instant friendship with Anne, recognizing her as a kindred spirit. Soon after, Anne introduced Stephen Irving's young son Paul to her, and the two formed a warm bond. Anne subsequently facilitated a meeting between Stephen and Miss Lavendar when Stephen returned to Prince Edward Island. Resolving their long-standing misunderstanding, Stephen proposed, and the two were married in her garden under the honeysuckle arbor before moving to Boston. They returned to Echo Lodge each summer to vacation and entertain their friends.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert and Matthew decide to adopt an orphan boy.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert and her brother Matthew decide to adopt an orphan boy to help with farm work, but due to a misunderstanding, Anne Shirley is brought to Green Gables instead. Though initially determined to send the girl back, Marilla relents out of pity and a sense of duty, agreeing to raise her. Over time, despite frequent trials caused by Anne's impulsive nature and vivid imagination, Marilla grows deeply affectionate toward her. When Matthew dies suddenly, Marilla faces severe failing eyesight and considers selling Green Gables, but Anne decides to stay in Avonlea to help her keep the homestead. Later, Marilla takes in the orphaned twins Davy and Dora Keith, eventually receiving a trust fund for their care. After Anne departs for college, Marilla invites Mrs. Rachel Lynde to live with her at Green Gables for companionship and shared duties.

unit: Marilla Cuthbert and her brother Matthew decide to adopt an orphan boy to help with farm work, but due to a misunderstanding, Anne Shirley is brought to Green Gables instead. Though initially determined to send the girl back, Marilla relents out of pity and a sense of duty, agreeing to raise her. Over time, despite frequent trials caused by Anne's impulsive nature and vivid imagination, Marilla grows deeply affectionate toward her. When Matthew dies suddenly, Marilla faces severe failing eyesight and considers selling Green Gables, but Anne decides to stay in Avonlea to help her keep the homestead. Later, Marilla takes in the orphaned twins Davy and Dora Keith, eventually receiving a trust fund for their care. After Anne departs for college, Marilla invites Mrs. Rachel Lynde to live with her at Green Gables for companionship and shared duties.

label: Personality
value: Matthew is exceptionally shy.
unit: Matthew is exceptionally shy, quiet, and meek, dreading interactions with women and strangers and hating to go anywhere he might be forced to talk. Despite his reserve, he is deeply sympathetic, kind-hearted, and quietly persistent when he sets his mind on something. He enjoys listening to talkative people provided they do not expect him to speak, and he forms a warm, tender bond with Anne Shirley, whom he loves to spoil.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables with his sister Marilla and decided to adopt an orphan boy to help him with farm duties as his health declined. When he drove to Bright River station to collect the child, he unexpectedly found Anne Shirley instead and brought her home. Touched by her personality, Matthew quietly insisted on keeping her at Green Gables despite Marilla's initial reluctance. Over the years, he supported Anne, buying her a puffed-sleeve dress for Christmas and continuously expressing pride in her academic successes. As his heart condition worsened with age and overwork, he suffered a fatal shock upon reading of the failure of the Abbey Bank where the family savings were stored. Following his sudden death, he was buried in Avonlea, where Anne regularly visits his grave.

label: History
value: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea
unit: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea from the United States to live with his grandmother, Mrs. Irving, at the shore road. Upon joining the Avonlea school, he quickly forms a deep bond with his teacher, Anne Shirley, who recognizes his poetic genius and imaginative soul. Though well-liked by his classmates, he struggles secretly with his grandmother's strict diet of porridge and old-fashioned discipline. When Anne introduces him to Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge, Paul forms an instant affection for her. Later, Paul's father Stephen Irving unexpectedly visits Avonlea, reunites with Miss Lavendar, and marries her, giving Paul a second mother whom he fondly calls 'Mother Lavendar.' After the wedding, Paul moves to Boston with his father and stepmother, returning to Echo Lodge for summer vacations. As he grows older, he gradually leaves his childhood imaginary 'rock people' behind for games like football, while retaining his strong bond with Anne.

value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school, where he spent much of his time giving extra attention and lessons to Prissy Andrews, whom he openly courted. Early in Anne Shirley's school days, he humiliated her by forcing her to stand at the blackboard with her name misspelled after she struck Gilbert Blythe for teasing her. On a subsequent day, he singled Anne out for being late and ordered her to sit with Gilbert as punishment, prompting Anne to temporarily leave the school. After a period of initial friction, he praised Anne's academic progress to Matthew Cuthbert, though he continued to criticize her geometry skills. At the school concert, he recited Mark Antony's oration while directing his performance toward Prissy Andrews. He departed from his role at Avonlea school at the end of June, delivering an emotional farewell speech to the students before leaving town.

unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school, where he spent much of his time giving extra attention and lessons to Prissy Andrews, whom he openly courted. Early in Anne Shirley's school days, he humiliated her by forcing her to stand at the blackboard with her name misspelled after she struck Gilbert Blythe for teasing her. On a subsequent day, he singled Anne out for being late and ordered her to sit with Gilbert as punishment, prompting Anne to temporarily leave the school. After a period of initial friction, he praised Anne's academic progress to Matthew Cuthbert, though he continued to criticize her geometry skills. At the school concert, he recited Mark Antony's oration while directing his performance toward Prissy Andrews. He departed from his role at Avonlea school at the end of June, delivering an emotional farewell speech to the students before leaving town.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy in Charlottetown.
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy in Charlottetown, where she formed a close friendship with Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard. After completing her studies at Queen's, she was engaged to teach school at Carmody for a year before returning to teach at her home school. During this period, she visited Avonlea, participated in meetings for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society—writing papers for the group—and introduced her aunt, the famous writer Mrs. Charlotte E. Morgan, to her friends. Later, upon gaining her father's consent, Priscilla enrolled alongside Anne at Redmond College in Kingsport, where the two shared a boardinghouse. During their second year at college, Priscilla, Anne, Stella, and Philippa Gordon rented Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue, keeping house together under the care of Stella's Aunt Jamesina. Priscilla completed her degree at Redmond, reflecting on how much her college experience broadened her appreciation of life.

After completing her studies at Queen's, she was engaged to teach school at Carmody for a year before returning to teach at her home school. During this period, she visited Avonlea, participated in meetings for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society—writing papers for the group—and introduced her aunt, the famous writer Mrs. Charlotte E. Morgan, to her friends. Later, upon gaining her father's consent, Priscilla enrolled alongside Anne at Redmond College in Kingsport, where the two shared a boardinghouse. During their second year at college, Priscilla, Anne, Stella, and Philippa Gordon rented Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue, keeping house together under the care of Stella's Aunt Jamesina. Priscilla completed her degree at Redmond, reflecting on how much her college experience broadened her appreciation of life.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived with her husband, Thomas Lynde.
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived with her husband, Thomas Lynde, in Lynde's Hollow, where she kept watch over all passersby. When Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert decided to adopt a child, she openly voiced her doubts and disapproval. On her first visit to meet Anne Shirley, she criticized the orphan girl's physical appearance, sparking an outburst of anger from Anne; however, she forgave Anne after receiving a dramatic apology. She actively involved herself in community and church matters, running the Sewing Circle, aiding the Sunday school, and leading the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. Following the death of her husband, Thomas, and the realization that their mortgaged farm would have to be sold, Mrs. Rachel accepted Marilla Cuthbert's invitation to move into Green Gables rather than leave Avonlea. There, she set up her home in the former spare room and helped look after the twins, Davy and Dora.

label: History
value: Roy Gardner belonged to a family
unit: Roy Gardner belonged to an influential and wealthy family in Kingsport. He was forced to leave college for two years to travel abroad when his mother fell ill, but later returned to complete his studies at Redmond College. He first met Anne Shirley in a park during a rainstorm when he offered her shelter under his umbrella. Captivated by her, he began courting her attentively by sending flowers, poetry, and visiting her at Patty's Place. Though widely expected by college circles and his own family to marry Anne, Roy was rejected when he proposed to her in the park pavilion. Devastated by her refusal, he bade her farewell and accepted that they could not be together.

label: Appearance
value: Ruby was very handsome.
unit: Ruby was a very handsome girl with long, beautiful yellow-golden braids, large bright-blue eyes, a brilliant complexion, and a plump, showy figure. Toward the end of her life, galloping consumption made her very thin, with hectically bright cheeks and transparently delicate hands. After her death, her white-clad body possessed a pure, consecrated beauty that was remembered in Avonlea for years.

label: History
value: Ruby grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Ruby grew up in Avonlea as a schoolmate of Anne Shirley and Diana Barry. She attended Queen's Academy in the teacher's preparation class, earning her license alongside her friends. After graduating, she taught school at Carmody while returning home on weekends. She enjoyed a vibrant social life filled with numerous suitors, including Nelson Atkins, Wilbur Blair, and eventually Herb Spencer. During the winter, she suffered an attack of chest congestion that developed into galloping consumption. Unable to continue teaching, she hid her illness under a lively facade until her declining health forced her to accept the truth. She spent her final summer sharing intimate conversations with Anne in her garden before passing away peacefully in her sleep.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired as Avonlea's first female teacher.
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired as Avonlea's first female teacher, introducing various educational innovations such as biweekly recitation sessions, physical culture exercises, nature study field days, and composition practice. She organized a student concert on Christmas Night to raise funds for a schoolhouse flag. Recognizing potential in her advanced students, she formed an after-school class to prepare them for the Queen's Academy entrance examination. Though offered a job in her home district, she decided to return to Avonlea for a second year out of dedication to seeing her pupils through their entrance tests. Under her guidance, all of her Queen's candidates passed their exams, with Anne Shirley taking top honors. After ending her term at Avonlea, she later visited the area and remained a cherished friend and mentor to her former students.

value: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy, where she formed a close circle of friends with Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant. She came up with the idea to rent Patty's Place in Kingsport for their second year at Redmond, inviting her Aunt Jamesina to keep house for them and living alongside Anne, Priscilla, and Philippa Gordon. Stella continued her studies at Redmond, participating in campus activities like the Philomathic Society, and successfully passed her final examinations alongside her housemates.

She came up with the idea to rent Patty's Place in Kingsport for their second year at Redmond, inviting her Aunt Jamesina to keep house for them and living alongside Anne, Priscilla, and Philippa Gordon. Stella continued her studies at Redmond, participating in campus activities like the Philomathic Society, and successfully passed her final examinations alongside her housemates.
